title: Regular sequences f_i x_i in a polynomial ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$ elements which do not generate the unit ideal. The following are equivalent: (1) every permutation of $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; (2) every subsequence $f_{i_1},\dots,f_{i_s}$ ($i_1<\dots<i_s$) is a regular sequence in $R$; (3) $f_1x_1,\dots,f_rx_r$ is a regular sequence in the polynomial ring $R[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

proof.text:
(2)$\Rightarrow$(1), by induction on $r$, the claim for $r$ being: for every family of $r$ elements of $R$ not generating the unit ideal, (2) implies (1). For $r\le1$, (1) and (2) say the same (that $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor, resp. nothing beyond $R
e0$). Let $r\ge2$, assume (2) for $f_1,\dots,f_r$ and let $\sigma$ be a permutation; put $s=\sigma(r)$. Every subfamily of $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in the given order again satisfies (2) (its subsequences are subsequences of $f_1,\dots,f_r$) and does not generate the unit ideal. Hence by the induction hypothesis applied to the $r-1$ elements $f_j$, $j
e s$ (in increasing order of $j$), the permutation $f_{\sigma(1)},\dots,f_{\sigma(r-1)}$ of them is a regular sequence. Since $(f_{\sigma(1)},\dots,f_{\sigma(r-1)})=(f_j:j
e s)$ and $R/(f_1,\dots,f_r)
e0$, it remains to show that $f_s$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/(f_j:j
e s)$. If $s=r$ this is the last condition of the regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$, given by (2).

proof.text:
The key computation for (3). Let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and for $0\le i\le r$ let $J_i=(f_1x_1,\dots,f_ix_i)\subset P$ and, for a multi-index $E$, $I_E=(f_j:1\le j\le i,\ e_j>0)\subset R$ (depending on $i$). By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ideal-coefficients-monomial], $\sum_Ec_Ex^E\in J_i$ iff $c_E\in I_E$ for all $E$. Claim: for $i<r$, multiplication by $f_{i+1}x_{i+1}$ is injective on $P/J_i$ iff $f_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/I_E$ for every $E$. Indeed, let $\varepsilon$ be the $(i+1)$-st unit multi-index; then $f_{i+1}x_{i+1}\sum_Ec_Ex^E=\sum_E f_{i+1}c_Ex^{E+\varepsilon}$, and $I_{E+\varepsilon}=I_E$ because $i+1>i$ does not enter $I_E$. So $f_{i+1}x_{i+1}p\in J_i$ iff $f_{i+1}c_E\in I_E$ for all $E$. If $f_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on every $R/I_E$, this gives $c_E\in I_E$ for all $E$, i.e. $p\in J_i$; conversely if $f_{i+1}c\in I_E$ with $c
otin I_E$ for some $E$, then $p=cx^E

e0$ in $R$, so $1

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DW (lemma-regular-sequence-in-polynomial-ring), second paragraph (direct sum decomposition; Stacks writes $f_{i+1}x_i$, a misprint for $f_{i+1}x_{i+1}$)

proof.text: (3)$\Rightarrow$(2). Let $f_{i_1},\dots,f_{i_s}$ ($i_1<\dots<i_s$) be a subsequence and $1\le t\le s$. Apply (3) at the index $i=i_t-1$: $f_{i_t}x_{i_t}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $P/J_{i_t-1}$, so by the previous step $f_{i_t}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/I_E$ for every $E$. Take $E$ with $e_j=1$ for $j\in\{i_1,\dots,i_{t-1}\}$ and $e_j=0$ otherwise; since these $j$ are $\le i_t-1$, $I_E=(f_{i_1},\dots,f_{i_{t-1}})$. Thus $f_{i_t}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/(f_{i_1},\dots,f_{i_{t-1}})$ for all $t$, and $R/(f_{i_1},\dots,f_{i_s})\ne0$ (first step), so the subsequence is regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. (Stacks takes only $E$ with all entries positive, which gives the full sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$; the choice of $E$ with support $\{i_1,\dots,i_{t-1}\}$ gives every subsequence.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DW (lemma-regular-sequence-in-polynomial-ring), (3) implies (2)

proof.text: (2)$\Rightarrow$(3). Let $0\le i<r$ and $E$ a multi-index; let $j_1<\dots<j_q$ be the indices $j\le i$ with $e_j>0$, so $I_E=(f_{j_1},\dots,f_{j_q})$. The subsequence $f_{j_1},\dots,f_{j_q},f_{i+1}$ is regular by (2), so $f_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/I_E$. By the key computation, $f_{i+1}x_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $P/J_i=P/(f_1x_1,\dots,f_ix_i)P$ for every $i<r$ (for $i=0$: on $P$), and $P/J_r\ne0$. Hence $f_1x_1,\dots,f_rx_r$ is a regular sequence in $P$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Algebra Tag 07DW (verbatim up to notation; kept). Proof follows the Stacks proof in six steps: (1)=>(2) elementary from the definition; (2)=>(1) by induction on r with the length-2 swap (new node lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-swap-two, the 'clear' case r=2 of the Stacks proof) applied in R/(f_j : j<=r-1, j!=s); the monomial description of R[x]/(f_1x_1,...,f_ix_i) (new node lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ideal-coefficients-monomial) and the resulting criterion for f_{i+1}x_{i+1} to be a nonzerodivisor; (3)=>(2) and (2)=>(3). Corrected two points of the Stacks text: f_{i+1}x_i is a misprint for f_{i+1}x_{i+1}; Stacks's (3)=>(2) takes only E with all entries positive, which yields only the full sequence, and the step uses E supported on the subsequence to get every subsequence. Stacks cites no lemma in this proof. Mathlib: RegularSequence.lean has an explicit TODO for 07DW; no leaf. The citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-char-p uses (1)=>(3).

reviewed.note: 6 steps following Stacks 07DW with two corrections (misprint f_{i+1}x_i; (3)=>(2) needs multi-indices supported on the subsequence to get every subsequence). (2)=>(1) by induction with the swap lemma (new node: a,b regular and b a nonzerodivisor => b,a regular); (3) via the new node on coefficients of (g_1x_1,...,g_ix_i) (P/J = direct sum of R/I_E x^E). Checked steps 2-6. Mathlib has a TODO for 07DW (RegularSequence.lean:590).
